Text.Text: You know the rule of my counter by now: if you're standing there, you're holding something. Here - keep that level while I titrate. The sublevel under the Coral Isles drains clean these days, the clinics in Dac City got their kolto back, and the only one building an emergency cocktail now is you, when someone's dying and the minutes run short. That's how it should be. I even slept last week. Don't spread that around.

Careful - don't touch that rack. Your reach says confidence, but your hands say first aid isn't finished with you yet. The craft has layers under the ones you've learned, and I only teach the last one. Wring everything out of the wards first - every technique, every hour they'll give you. When there's nothing left up there to learn, come back to my counter. I'll still be awake.

Hold this vial - level, don't tilt it, it's mid-titration and I don't own a spare. Good. You have working hands, so listen. There's a crew in the Medical Sublevel on Mon Cala running my discipline backwards: hot stabilizer batches, mixed fast, tested on patients who can't crawl off the cot. Their adepts hold the arms down. Put six of them down instead, and bring me the book they log the doses in - the Emergency Cocktail Triage Ward Ledger. My format, their handwriting. I want it off their counter and onto mine.

Take the key off that hook - the one with the red tag. It works the service lift down to the Medical Sublevel. On Mon Cala, go east from Dac City through the Coral Isles to the facility on the south-west side of the outer isles. Eco-terrorists hold it, but you won't have to go far: take the sliding door off the entry hall, and the lift stands in the red-walled bay just east of the office block. Six adepts, one ledger, and don't drink anything you find in an unmarked flask. Minutes matter more the longer you stand here.

A stabilizer you build under fire. No clean bench, no scale, no second try - just what's in your kit and a patient losing the argument with their own blood pressure. Done right, it buys minutes that don't exist. Done the way that crew does it, it's a coin flip with someone else's heart. That's the difference you're going down there to enforce.

Mon Cala. From the landing at the "Elite" Hotel in Dac City, go out through the surface streets and east into the Coral Isles - the inner isles, then the outer. On the south-west side of the outer isles is the Coral Isles Facility. Eco-terrorists hold it, so keep your head down. Go through the sliding door off the entry hall; the service lift stands in the red-walled bay just east of the office block. It runs down to the facility's old medical station. That's the Medical Sublevel.

Chemists who stopped asking permission. The adepts are dosed on their own product - faster than they should be, numb where you'd hope they weren't. They'll come at you with blasters and injectors, and if one grabs you, count your pulse, because whatever's in the syringe works in seconds. Keep your kit stocked and your exits counted.
The ledger's still down there, and so are the six adepts writing in it. Every hour you spend up here, that book gains a page. Go.
That smell - antiseptic and scorched sugar. You found their counter. Hand the ledger over before I say something grateful.

Forty doses in nine days, initialed like it's something to be proud of. Six sets of initials that won't appear again, thanks to you. Credits are in the drawer - hazard rate, because I'm not insulting either of us. When your hands have recovered, come back. The next lesson costs more.

You again. Good - hold this coupler housing while I talk, it wants a steady grip. The crew took the ledger loss badly. Their specialists have spliced feed lines straight into the sublevel's kolto conduits: raw kolto into hot batches, no filtration, straight into whoever's strapped down. Five specialists run the splice. Take them apart and bring me the fitting itself - the Emergency Cocktail Kolto Conduit Coupler. Without it their whole draw collapses, and I get proof of exactly what they tapped.

Same facility, same key. The specialists work the kolto lines all over the sublevel. Cut them away before they can vent anything at you, and bring the coupler back intact. A cracked one tells me nothing except that you were careless.

An adept holds the arm. A specialist decides what goes into it. They trained under real ward staff before they went below, which means they know dosage, timing, and precisely how much a body can take before it stops complaining. They will use all three on you.

Because a splice fitting is a signature. The coupler will show the machining, the batch residue, the draw rate - enough for me to prove to the healers in Dac City that the kolto meant for their clinics ran the operation. The ledger told me what they did. The coupler tells me what it cost the clinics in the city.

Rougher than last time. The specialists work in pairs and they don't panic - panic is for people who haven't already decided you're a test subject. They like to fight near the kolto lines, and whatever they throw at you isn't medicine. Go in rested. That's a prescription, not a suggestion.
Five specialists, one coupler, and a kolto line bleeding into bad batches the whole time you're up here. The math doesn't pause. Neither should you.
You're carrying something heavy and machined, and your jacket smells like kolto steam. That's my coupler. Counter. Now.

Look at this draw gauge - they were pulling triple what a clinic pulls in a full emergency, around the clock. This goes to the healers in Dac City with my compliments and your fingerprints wiped off. Credits in the drawer. You're becoming a line item in my budget, which is the closest thing to affection I keep in stock.

Put the tray down and listen, because this one changes the dosage. In the sublevel's south-west wing, the crew keeps its clean room, where the real batches get made. Their warden holds it. Ward-trained, dosed to the eyes, and mean enough that the specialists knock. I want him gone and the Emergency Cocktail Fractured Ward Sigil back in my hands. And you don't go alone. That's triage math: one of you bleeds out in that room, three of you walk out. Bring two you'd trust with your airway.

Good answer - the plural was the part I was checking. The clean room is in the south-west wing of the sublevel. Hit the warden fast, keep someone breathing between injectors, and take the sigil off him when it's done. I'll have three stims and a strong opinion waiting.

He ran a trauma ward in Dac City for six years. Best hands I ever watched work - and then he decided consent was a bottleneck. Now he guards their clean room and doses himself from the stock. Whatever speed and strength you're imagining, add more, and remember he knows exactly where you keep your arteries. Professionally.

Simple sums. One fighter in that room means the warden picks when you rest, when you bleed, and when it ends. Two means someone can drag the other clear. Three means he has to choose, and choosing is where fights get lost. I've run this arithmetic on cot after cot for twenty years. Bring two companions, or don't bring yourself.

It marked that clean room as a sanctioned ward - the matron's mark, from when the sublevel still healed people. The crew cracked it when they took the room, and the warden kept the broken half like a joke. Bring it to me. I'd rather it sit broken in my drawer than in his pocket.
The warden's still holding the clean room, and if you're standing here alone, you're still two people short of a survivable entry. Gather your trusted pair, then go take that sigil off him.
You're moving like someone who got hit hard and treated fast - which means your companions did their jobs. Is that the sigil? Give it here.

There's the crack, right through the ward mark. They wanted the joke on record; now it's evidence. The clean room's dark, the warden's off the board, and Dac City owes you more than what's in my drawer - but the drawer is what I control, so take it. And tell your two they have standing credit at my counter. That's not nothing.

Sit. I already poured you a stimulant - that's how you know it's serious. With the warden gone, the crew's core came up from hiding. Four of them, the inner circle, the ones who wrote the hot-batch doctrine. More implant than patient now. They're walking the sublevel like they own it, and they carry the Emergency Cocktail Matron's Ward Token, the old matron's own mark of care, pocketed like a trophy. Four names, one token. Bring it back.

They don't keep to one room anymore - they walk the sublevel checking on what's left of their operation. Find them one at a time if you can. Keep your companions close; four trained sets of hands against one of yours is arithmetic I've already given you my opinion on.

The founders. Two washed out of medical certification in Dac City, one mixed for a mercenary column, and the fourth - the fourth trained me, years ago, which is a sentence I'd rather you forgot. They've each replaced so much of themselves you'd need a mechanic to find the original patient. Every dose in that ledger traces uphill to those four signatures.

Before the eco-terrorists took the facility above, the sublevel's wards answered to a matron, healing divers and isle crews nobody else would take. Whoever held her token answered for every patient below. The circle took it because holding it says the sublevel answers to them. I don't run on sentiment, but I make an exception for that piece of brass.

Four practitioners who've each survived their own doctrine, wired with enough hardware to shrug off what would drop you. If they find you together, they'll stagger their injectors so one is always fresh. If your two from the warden fight are still upright, this is where you spend that trust again. Don't trade one-for-one with people who keep spares.
The circle is still walking the sublevel, and the token is still in the wrong pocket. Four names. I've crossed out none of them yet.
Your hands are steadier than mine tonight, and that's a first for this counter. Show me the token.

Brass, and lighter than its job description. Four signatures closed out, and the matron's mark comes home. I'd call that a good shift, and I haven't called anything a good shift in two years. Credits in the drawer. Rest and restock - the Protected Ward is still lit, and we both know who's in it.

No tray this time. Both hands free, because you should hear this straight. The one left is the master - the chemist the circle answered to. He perfected the emergency cocktail: he can build a stabilizer from pocket vials mid-fight and pull himself back from the edge, over and over. It cost a wing full of patients to refine. He's holed up in the Protected Ward, reached from the north-east corner of the sublevel. Kill him, and I'll teach you the recipe built clean. Taken alone, his room is a lethal dose. Take your two, or take more.

Then go, and keep each other breathing. The way into the Protected Ward is in the north-east corner of the sublevel, and he'll know you're coming - he's been reading the same ledger entries backwards. When he goes down, don't collect anything. Walk back up breathing. That's the only proof I need.

An entire recovery wing. Twenty-six beds. He needed subjects at the exact edge of death to tune the timing, so he manufactured the edge. The cocktail works - that's the unbearable part. Every one of those patients stabilized beautifully, right up until he needed the bed for the next iteration. Perfection with a body count. That's what you're ending.

Because I already tried. Years ago, when it was him and me and one shared bench. I ran, he stayed, and everything at the bottom of that lift is what staying looks like. My hands still mix a fair cocktail, but they shake when that door comes up in conversation, and shaking hands kill patients. You're my steady hands now. That's the whole confession - don't make me repeat it.

Like a man who has never once worried about dying, because for him it's a solved problem. He'll take wounds that should end it, drink his own work, and stand back up with his pulse reset. You can't out-wait him alone and you can't out-bleed him alone. Three of you, rotating, wearing him down between doses - the recipe has a seam, and the seam is minutes. Spend yours better than he spends his.
The Protected Ward is still lit. Take your people, go through the north-east corner of the sublevel, and put the recipe out of his hands. I'll be awake. I'm always awake.
You walked in slow, and you're not carrying anything - which, this one time, is exactly right. Tell me it's done.

Then sit down, because class starts now. The emergency cocktail, built clean - no strapped-down subjects, no forced doses, no ledger. Just your kit, your minutes, and hands I've watched earn this one stage at a time. He perfected it on other people's blood; you'll carry it on your own. That distinction is the entire discipline. Take a stool. First lesson: nothing you build under fire is ever for you.

The Medshed on Smuggler's Moon needed working hands. I needed a counter where the next patient could reach me without a Republic escort. I don't check allegiance before I stop bleeding. The crew is in the Medical Sublevel under the Coral Isles Facility on Mon Cala - nobody's army holds it, just eco-terrorists squatting on top. Bring their dose records back to this counter.
Back to the job.
Give me the way down. I'll get your ledger.
What is an emergency cocktail, exactly?
How do I reach this sublevel?
What's waiting for me down there?
Not today. Find another set of hands.
Their Triage Ward Ledger. Every dose is in it.
Back to the specialists.
Five specialists. I'll bring you the coupler.
What makes a specialist worse than an adept?
Why does the coupler matter so much?
How rough will it get down there this time?
My kit's empty. I'll come back restocked.
One Kolto Conduit Coupler, mostly intact.
Back to the warden.
I'll find two I trust and put the warden down.
Who is this warden?
Walk me through your triage math.
What's the ward sigil to you?
Not until I have the right people beside me.
The Fractured Ward Sigil. The warden won't miss it.
Back to the circle.
Four of them, one token. Done.
Who are these four?
What's the matron's token to the sublevel?
Four at once. What am I walking into?
Let me settle my nerves first.
The Matron's Ward Token. The circle is finished.
Back to the master.
We go down together, and I'll finish it.
What did perfecting it cost him?
Why haven't you gone down there yourself?
How does he fight?
Not yet. This one deserves my best.
He's dead. The recipe is ours now.
Why are we meeting here, and where is the trial?
Back to the assignment.
